The '''2014–15 season''' was '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona's]]''' 116th in existence and the club's [[All-Time La Liga table|84th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football. This was the first of the three seasons under head coach [[Luis Enrique]].

The season was one of the most successful ones in the club's history, as Barcelona clinched its second [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]] after winning La Liga, the Copa del Rey and the UEFA Champions League. The league title was won in a closely fought title race with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], while the Copa victory was achieved with a brilliant 3–1 victory over [[Athletic Bilbao]] at Camp Nou in the final. In the Champions League, Barcelona overcame [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] (3–0 home, 2–3 away) to set up the final against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in Berlin, where Barça triumphed 3–1. Barcelona's success may be in large part attributed to their formidable attacking trio composed of [[Lionel Messi]], [[Neymar]], and summer signing [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]], who scored a record 122 goals in all competitions to become the trio with most goals in a single season in Spanish football history.

The season was the first since [[1998–99 FC Barcelona season|1998–99]] without former captain [[Carles Puyol]], who retired at the end of [[2013–14 FC Barcelona season|last season]], [[2001–02 FC Barcelona season|2001–02]], and [[2006–07 FC Barcelona season|2006–07]] without goalkeepers [[Víctor Valdés]] and [[José Manuel Pinto]]. Valdés joined [[2014–15 Manchester United F.C. season|Manchester United]] in January 2015; whereas Pinto announced his retirement.

==Season overview==
===May===
At the end of the [[2013–14 FC Barcelona season]], goalkeepers [[José Manuel Pinto]] and [[Víctor Valdés]] expired contracts were not renewed. Barcelona quickly signed [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] from [[Bundesliga]] club [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], and [[Claudio Bravo]] from fellow [[La Liga]] outfit [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/ter-stegen-arrives-pinto-leaves |title=Goalkeeping changes for new season. |publisher=FCBacelona.com |date=19 May 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-for-claudio-bravo-to-join-fc-barcelona |title=Goalkeeping changes for new season. |publisher=FCBacelona.com |date=25 June 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref> On 15 May, long-time [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Carles Puyol]] announced his retirement from football after a 15-year career on the first team.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/puyol-i-came-here-as-a-boy-and-i-leave-with-a-family |title=Puyol bids farewell after 15 years. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=15 May 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref> Puyol was subsequently named Assistant to Sports Management under [[Director of football]] [[Andoni Zubizarreta]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/season/2013-2014/carles-puyol-new-assistant-to-sports-management |title=Puyol to remain at Barça in the Football Department. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=31 May 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref> On 19 May, [[Luis Enrique]] was named the new manager after it was announced that [[Gerardo Martino]] would step down at the end of the season. Luis Enrique returned to Barça after being the [[Barcelona B|B Team]] manager from 2008 to 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/luis-enrique-signs-two-year-deal-as-new-fc-barcelona-manager |title=Luis Enrique becomes new manager. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 May 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref>

===June===
On 12 June, Barcelona and [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] reached an agreement for the transfer of [[midfielder]] [[Cesc Fàbregas]] for a reported fee of €33&nbsp;million. With the move, Fàbregas returned to London where he started his first team career as an [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] player.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-chelsea-for-the-transfer-of-cesc-fabregas |title=Fàbregas moves to Chelsea. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=12 June 2014 |access-date= 7 July 2014}}</ref> On 16 June, Barcelona signed [[Croats|Croatian]] midfielder [[Ivan Rakitić]] from [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] for €18&nbsp;million along with the loan of [[FC Barcelona B|Barcelona B]] midfielder [[Denis Suárez]] for the next two seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-ivan-rakitic-join-fc-barcelona |title=Rakitić joined Barcelona. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=16 June 2014 |access-date=7 July 2014}}</ref> Rakitić joins after leading Sevilla to the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League]] title, where he was named [[man of the match]] in the [[2014 UEFA Europa League Final|final]].

===July===
On 9 July, Barcelona announced the transfer of [[Jonathan dos Santos]] to [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] for a fee of €2&nbsp;million. Most of his last season with the club was spent recovering from an [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL tear]] which he suffered in training on 23 October 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-with-villarreal-for-the-services-of-jonathan-dos-santos |title=Dos Santos moves to Villarreal. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=9 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> With the move, Jonathan reunited with his older brother [[Giovani dos Santos]], since both players shared time on the Barcelona youth team. On 10 July, Barcelona announced it had rescinded the contract of [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Isaac Cuenca]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-to-rescind-isaac-cuenca-s-contract |title=Barça rescind Cuenca's contract |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Cuenca then made the move to [[Deportivo de La Coruña]], where he signed for one season to join the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galician]] club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.canaldeportivo.com/servlet/es.iris.servlets.Noticias?accion=4&ver=1&nid=28304&mid=12 |title=Cuenca signs with Deportivo la Coruña. |publisher=CanalDeportivo.com |language=es |date=10 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Later in the day, Barcelona completed the transfer of [[Alexis Sánchez]] to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] for €42&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-agree-terms-with-arsenal-for-alexis-sanchez |title=Sánchez completes move to Arsenal. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 July 2014 |access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Sánchez left after three years when he had played 141 matches and scored 47 goals, including a season personal best of 21 goals during the 2013–14 season.

On 11 July, Barcelona and [[England|English]] club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] announced the transfer of [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguayan international]] forward [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] for a reported fee of £75&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-and-liverpool-fc-have-reached-an-agreement-for-the-transfer-of-luis-suarez |title=Suárez joins Barça. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 July 2014 |access-date=30 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712034551/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-and-liverpool-fc-have-reached-an-agreement-for-the-transfer-of-luis-suarez |archive-date=12 July 2014 }}</ref> The reigning [[European Golden Shoe]] winner joined after spending four seasons with the [[Merseyside]] club in which he scored 82 goals in 133 appearances. Barcelona were without Suárez's services after the [[FIFA Disciplinary Code|FIFA Disciplinary Committee]] banned the player for four months of any football-related activity after he was found guilty of [[List of 2014 FIFA World Cup controversies#Uruguay vs Italy|biting Italian defender Giorgio Chiellini]] during Uruguay's [[2014 FIFA World Cup Group D#Italy vs Uruguay|final World Cup group stage match]]. The suspension meant Suárez was unable to play for Barcelona until 26 October.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=luis-suarez-suspended-for-nine-matches-and-banned-for-four-months-from-2386354.html |title=Suárez suspended for 4-months from all football-related activity. |publisher=FIFA.com |date=26 June 2014 |access-date=15 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703172739/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y%3D2014/m%3D6/news%3Dluis-suarez-suspended-for-nine-matches-and-banned-for-four-months-from-2386354.html |archive-date=3 July 2014 }}</ref> Later in the day, [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Oier Olazábal|Oier]] moved to [[Granada CF|Granada]] on a free transfer to the [[Andalusia]]n club. The transfer, however, included the caveat that "Barcelona reserves the economic rights to any future transfer of the player".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/goalkeeper-oier-olazabal-transferred-to-granada|title=Oier Olazabal completes move to Granada.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=11 July 2014|access-date=11 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140815034429/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/goalkeeper-oier-olazabal-transferred-to-granada|archive-date=15 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 16 July, Barcelona announced that [[Spain national football team|Spanish]] [[Forward (association football)#Winger|winger]] [[Cristian Tello]] would be moving on a two-year [[Loan (sports)|loan]] deal to [[Portugal|Portuguese]] club [[FC Porto|Porto]] for a loan fee of €2&nbsp;million. The deal included a purchase option for Porto of €8&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/cristian-tello-loaned-to-porto |title=Tello makes move to Porto. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=16 July 2014 |access-date=18 July 2014}}</ref> Barcelona also informed that [[left back]] [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] would be out four-to-six weeks with an abnormal heart rhythm discovered during his return medical.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/adriano-correia-out-for-4-to-6-weeks |title=Adriano out 4 to 6 weeks. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=16 July 2014 |access-date=18 July 2014}}</ref> On 19 July, Barcelona played their first friendly of the pre-season against [[Recreativo de Huelva]] at the [[Nuevo Colombino]] in [[Huelva]]. The match ended 0–1 with the only goal coming from Barcelona B winger [[Joan Àngel Román]] in the 66th minute that gave Barça the [[Trofeo Colombino]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/amistoso/recreativo_fc-barcelona |title=Barça start off the pre-season on a winning note. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=19 July 2014 |access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref>

On 22 July, Barcelona parted ways with [[La Masia]] graduate and youth system all-time leading scorer [[Bojan Krkić|Bojan]]. Bojan moved to English club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] where he joined fellow La Masia graduate [[Marc Muniesa]] and ex-Barça striker and current manager [[Mark Hughes]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-for-bojan |title=Bojan set for Premier League football. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=22 July 2014 |access-date=24 July 2014}}</ref> On 23 July, Barcelona announced the transfer of [[France national football team|French international]] [[Defender (association football)|central defender]] [[Jérémy Mathieu]] from [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] for a transfer fee of €20&nbsp;million. Mathieu signed a contract for four seasons, with an optional season, and a buyout fee of €50&nbsp;million. With the move, Mathieu became the most expensive defender over 30 years old to be transferred.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/mathieu-veterano-record-3402744 |title=Mathieu, a veteran record. |publisher=SPORT.es |language=es |date=23 July 2014 |access-date=24 July 2014}}</ref>

===August===
On 9 August, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Belgium national football team|Belgium international]] defender [[Thomas Vermaelen]] from Arsenal for a fee of €19&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web |title=Agreement for Thomas Vermaelen to join FC Barcelona. |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-for-thomas-vermaelen-to-join-fc-barcelona |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=9 August 2014 |date=9 August 2014}}</ref> The next day, Barcelona also announced that [[Ibrahim Afellay]] would be headed to [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] in the [[Super League Greece]] for a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/afellay-loaned-to-olympiakos |title=Afellay sent to Olympiacos on season loan. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=10 August 2014}}</ref> On 14 August, the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS) confirmed the ban imposed by FIFA against Suárez, who remains suspended from football for four months, as well as a nine international match ban. However, the CAS removed the player's "football-related activities" ban, and was allowed to train with Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tas-cas.org/en/infogenerales.asp/4-3-7637-1092-4-1-1/5-0-1092-15-1-1/ |title=CAS upholds Suáre's ban. |publisher=TAS-CAS.org |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=18 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819224553/http://www.tas-cas.org/en/infogenerales.asp/4-3-7637-1092-4-1-1/5-0-1092-15-1-1 |archive-date=19 August 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Barcelona also announced it had reached an agreement with Sevilla for the loan of forward [[Gerard Deulofeu]] for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/agreement-in-principle-with-sevilla-fc-for-loan-of-gerard-deulofeu |title=Deulofeu loaned to Sevilla. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=18 August 2014}}</ref>

On 19 August, the [[FIFA]] Appeal Committee upheld its transfer ban on Barcelona in regards to "breaches relating to the international transfer and registration of players under the age of 18."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2313003/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140404202756/http://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2313003/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 April 2014 |title=Barcelona banned by FIFA from transferring players. |publisher=2 April 2014 |access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> Barcelona will be unable to transfer players during both the 2015 winter and summer transfer windows.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2423945/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821210207/http://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/organisation/news/newsid=2423945/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 August 2014 |title=Barcelona transfer ban upheld by FIFA. |publisher=FIFA.com |date=20 August 2014 |access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> Barcelona released a statement stating "that it shall continue defending its interests before the highest sporting authority, in this case the CAS".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/fc-barcelona-to-appeal-to-cas-following-fifa-resolution |title=Barça to continue fighting its transfer ban. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=20 August 2014 |access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> On 24 August, Barcelona started the season campaign with a 3-0 victory over [[Elche CF|Elche]] at the [[Camp Nou]]. A brace by [[Lionel Messi]] and a third by youth player [[Munir El Haddadi|Munir]] sealed the win for the ''Blaugrana''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-1/fc-barcelona_elche |title=Barça off with a win. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 August 2014 |access-date=26 August 2014}}</ref> On 27 August, Barcelona announced it had reached an agreement with [[Brazilians|Brazilian]] club [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] for the transfer of [[right-back]] [[Douglas (footballer, born August 1990)|Douglas]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/initial-agreement-for-douglas-pereira |title=Barça add São Paulo's Douglas. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=27 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref>

On 30 August, Barcelona and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] announced the loan for [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroonian international]] [[Alex Song]] for the remainder of the season to the Premier League club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/alex-song-loaned-to-west-ham |title=Loan spell for Song at West Ham. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 August 2014 |access-date=30 August 2014}}</ref> The next day, Barcelona won their first away match at [[Estadio de la Cerámica|El Madrigal]] 0–1 versus Villarreal with the lone goal scored by Barça B forward [[Sandro Ramírez|Sandro]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-2/villarreal_fc-barcelona |title=Villarreal 0–1 Barça |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 September 2014 |access-date=5 September 2014}}</ref>

===September===
{{Football kit box

On 13 September, Barcelona played their first match after the FIFA international break and for the first time in their history, wore their [[Senyera]] shirts from [[2013–14 FC Barcelona season|the previous season]] in a home game. The Senyera was used to commemorate the 300th anniversary of the [[Siege of Barcelona (1713–14)|Siege of Barcelona]] in 1714.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-to-wear-senyera-kit-against-bilbao |title=Barça to wear the Senyera at home. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 September 2014 |access-date=15 September 2014}}</ref> The match finished 2–0 victory against [[Athletic Bilbao]] with two second half goals from [[Neymar]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-3/fc-barcelona_athletic-club |title=Barça win it late. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=13 September 2014 |access-date=15 September 2014}}</ref> On 17 September, Barcelona played their first match in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage|2014–15 UEFA Champions League edition]] against [[2013–14 Cypriot First Division|Cypriot champions]] [[APOEL FC|APOEL]]. It was the official debut of youngster [[Sergi Samper]] for the first team and the 300th match for [[Dani Alves]] at Barcelona. Barça won the match 1–0 with [[Lionel Messi]] heading the winning goal in 28th minute. Piqué was named Man of the Match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2014309--barcelona-vs-apoel/ |title=Piqué the head boy as Barça edge past APOEL. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=17 September 2014 |access-date=17 September 2014}}</ref>

On 21 September, Barcelona played against [[Levante UD|Levante]]. Goals from Neymar, Ivan Rakitić, Sandro, [[Pedro (footballer, born 1987)|Pedro]] and Messi ensured that Barcelona had maintained their perfect record.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-4/llevant-u-d-_fc-barcelona|title=Barça maintains 100% record. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 September 2014 |access-date=21 September 2014}}</ref> On 24 September, Barcelona took on [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] at [[La Rosaleda Stadium|La Rosaleda]]. It was the debut match for [[Douglas (footballer, born August 1990)|Douglas]]. Barcelona dropped first point of the season in La Liga as the game ended as a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-5/malaga_fc-barcelona|title=Barça dropped first point. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=24 September 2014 |access-date=24 September 2014}}</ref> On 27 September, Barcelona played against [[Granada CF|Granada]] at Camp Nou. Barcelona kept up home form with a big win thanks to Neymar's first hat-trick of the season and a brace from Messi; the other goal came from Rakitić.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-6/fc-barcelona_granada-c-f|title=Neymar scored first hat-trick off the season. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=27 September 2014 |access-date=27 September 2014}}</ref> On 30 September, Barcelona played its second match in the Champions League, against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] at the [[Parc des Princes]]. It was the first defeat of the season and also the first time in the season Barça conceded a goal; PSG won 3–2, were goals from Messi and Neymar were not enough to escape defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2014333--paris-vs-barcelona/ |title=Barca experienced defeat at Paris. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=30 September 2014 |access-date=30 September 2014}}</ref>

===October===
On 4 October, Barcelona played [[Rayo Vallecano]] at the [[Campo de Fútbol de Vallecas|Campo de Vallecas]]. In an eventual 0–2 win with goals from Messi and Neymar,<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/rayo-vallecano-fc-barcelona-messi-and-neymar-on-target-again-0-2|title=Messi and Neymar on target again. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=4 October 2014 |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> goalkeeper [[Claudio Bravo]] made La Liga history by going 630 minutes without conceding a goal, surpassing former Barça goalkeeper [[Pedro María Artola]]'s record of 560 minutes, set in 1978.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2014/10/05/5158212/claudio-bravo-celebrates-barcelona-clean-sheet-record|title=Claudio Bravo's clean sheet record. |publisher=Goal.com |date=4 October 2014 |access-date=4 October 2014}}</ref> After an international break, Barcelona faced [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] at Camp Nou on 18 October. Barça won the match 3–0, with late goals from Messi, Neymar and [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-sd-eibar-3-0-second-half-firepower-sees-off-eibar|title=Second half firepower sees off Eibar|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 October 2014 |access-date=11 April 2015}}</ref> On 21 October, Barcelona hosted [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] at Camp Nou. Goals from Messi and Neymar and a late goal from youngster Sandro gave Barcelona a comfortable 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2014350--barcelona-vs-ajax/ |title=Barca's comfortable win at Camp Nou. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=21 October 2014 |access-date=21 October 2014}}</ref> On 25 October, Barcelona played the first ''[[El Clásico|Clásico]]'' of the season at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]]. This was the official debut match of star forward Luis Suárez due to his ban for biting [[Italy national football team|Italy]] defender [[Giorgio Chellini]] during the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]. Neymar gave Barcelona an early lead but Barcelona could not further capitalize on the lead; a converted penalty from [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and goals from [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] and [[Karim Benzema]] resulted in a 3–1 defeat. This was the first defeat for Barcelona in their 2014–15 Liga campaign.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/real-madrid-v-fc-barcelona-defeat-in-the-clasico-3-1|title=Defeat in first classico of the season. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 October 2014 |access-date=25 October 2014}}</ref> Claudio Bravo's clean sheet run ended at 754 minutes..

===November===
On 1 November, Barcelona played against [[Celta de Vigo]]. Barcelona's losing streak continued as they experienced their first home defeat of the season at Camp Nou; a single goal from [[Joaquín Larrivey]] decided the outcome of the match. Barça were down to the fourth position in the league table with the loss.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-10/fc-barcelona_celta-de-vigo|title=First home defeat of the season. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 November 2014 |access-date=1 November 2014}}</ref> On 5 November, Barca played against Ajax at [[Amsterdam Arena]]; Messi scored a brace as Barcelona won the match 0–2.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea72b5dd129-7e23781c9e16-1000--messi-matches-goal-record-as-barcelona-advance/ |title=Messi's double sent Barca to last 16. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=5 November 2014 |access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> With these two goals, Messi equalized the [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]]'s record as the all-time top scorer in the [[UEFA Champions League]].

On 8 November, Barcelona visited [[Estadio de los Juegos Mediterráneos|Juegos Mediterráneos]] to play against [[UD Almería|Almería]]. Barcelona earned a hard-fought win thanks to late goals from Neymar and [[Jordi Alba]] as [[Thievy Bifouma]] gave Almería the lead after 37 minutes. This win brought Barcelona to second in the table.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/ud-almeria-v-fc-barcelona-1-2-barca-make-late-comeback-and-win|title=Barca made late comeback. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 November 2014 |access-date=8 November 2014}}</ref> After the last international break of the year, Barça took on Sevilla at Camp Nou, winning 5–1 off goals by Neymar and Rakitić and a hat-trick from Messi, with Alba scoring an own goal.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-breaks-record-as-fc-barcelona-take-down-sevilla-by-the-horns-5-1|title=Barca took down sevilla by horns. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=22 November 2014 |access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref> With his second goal, Messi broke the record of [[Telmo Zarra]] to become the all-time top scorer of La Liga.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/88/spain/2014/11/22/6398141/messi-breaks-la-liga-goal-scoring-record|title=Messi broke La-liga's goal scoring record |publisher=Goal.com |date=22 November 2014 |access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref>

On 25 November, Barça won 0–4 against [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] at [[GSP Stadium]] of [[Nicosia]], [[Cyprus]]. Messi scored a hat-trick and Luis Suárez scored his first official goal for Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d7f92c2148b-b3d2e3311b15-1000--record-breaker-messi-leads-barca-stroll-at-apoel/ |title=Messi's hat-trick gave Barcelona convincing win. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=5 November 2014 |access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref> The hat-trick made Messi the all-time top scorer of the Champions League, surpassing Raúl.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d0421c873d6-e4d73ab1f2f2-1000--messi-breaks-raul-s-champions-league-goal-record/|title=Messi is the Champions League's top scorer. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=25 November 2014 |access-date=25 November 2014}}</ref> On 30 November, Barcelona earned a dramatic win against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] at [[Mestalla Stadium|Mestalla]] after an injury time goal from [[Sergio Busquets]] gave Barça the 0–1 win.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/valencia-cf-v-fc-barcelona-busquets-saves-the-day-0-1|title=Busquets saves Barcelona. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 November 2014 |access-date=30 November 2014}}</ref> At the time of celebrating the goal, Messi was struck by a bottle by a Valencia fan.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/374877.html|title=Messi struck by bottle. |work=ESPN.com |date=30 November 2014 |access-date=30 November 2014}}</ref> When Messi tried to report the incident to referee, he was shown a yellow card due to misunderstanding. Later on, due to the appeal from the club, the card was rescinded.

===December===
On 2 December, Barcelona defender Thomas Vermaelen, who was yet to make his official debut with Barcelona, underwent successful knee surgery in Finland. He would be out for next five-to-six months.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2014/12/02/6707632/vermaelen-surgery-a-success|title=Vermaelen undergo successful surgery. |publisher=Goal.com |date=2 December 2014 |access-date=2 December 2014}}</ref> Barcelona played the first match of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey]] against [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] at [[Estadio El Alcoraz]] on 3 December 2014. They won the round of 32 first leg by 0–4. Rakitić, [[Andrés Iniesta]], Pedro and [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] scored the goals. [[Luis Enrique]] rested many of first team starters and handed Barça B defender [[Edgar Ié]] his debut.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/sd-huesca-v-fc-barcelona-a-job-well-done-0-4|title=A nice start to cup. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=3 December 2014 |access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref> On 7 December, Barcelona played against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], the first [[Derbi barceloní|Catalan Derby]] of 2014–15 La Liga at Camp Nou. Espanyol took the lead by a goal from [[Sergio García (footballer, born 1983)|Sergio García]], but Barcelona eventually won the match 5–1 thanks to a hat-trick from Messi and goals from Piqué and Pedro.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/messi-and-barca-take-derby-against-espanyol-5-1|title=Win in Catalan Derby. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=7 December 2014 |access-date=7 December 2014}}</ref> On 10 December, Barca played last match of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage]], against Paris Saint-Germain at Camp Nou. The lead given by [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] for PSG did not last long, as goals from Messi, Neymar and Suárez gave Barcelona the 3–1 win, ensuring the top spot in [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Group F|Group F]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea6d97febe2-84c848b39884-1000--barcelona-win-group-f-ahead-of-paris/|title=Barca claimed top spot of group F. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=10 December 2014 |access-date=10 December 2014}}</ref> Barça played against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on 13 December at [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]]; the match ended in a goalless draw.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-15/getafe_fc-barcelona|title=Goalless draw at Getafe. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=13 December 2014 |access-date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

On 16 December, Barca played against [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] in the second leg of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Round of 32|Copa del Rey]] at Camp Nou. Huesca was thrashed 8–1 as Pedro scored a hat-trick and Barça B winger [[Adama Traoré (footballer, born 1996)|Adama Traoré]] scoring his first goal of the season for the first team. Other goalscorers were [[Sergi Roberto]], Iniesta, Adriano and Sandro. A goal from [[Carlos David Moreno|Carlos David]] only minimised the difference.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/copa-del-rey/1-16-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_sd-osca|title=Barca thrashed Huesca. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=16 December 2014 |access-date=16 December 2014}}</ref> By their 12–1 aggregate win, Barcelona are through to the last 16 of the Copa del Rey. Barça took on [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]] at Camp Nou on 20 December, the last match of the 2014 calendar year. Barcelona ended the year with a convincing 5–0 win off goals from Pedro, Suárez, Piqué and a late double from Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-cordoba-cf-five-goals-to-end-the-year-5-0|title=Five goals to end the year. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=20 December 2014 |access-date=20 December 2014}}</ref> On 30 December, Barça's appeal against two window transfer ban allotted by [[FIFA]] was rejected by [[Court of Arbitration for Sport|CAS]]. As a result, Barcelona will not be allowed to sign any new player until January 2016 and have to pay a fine of approximately €375,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2014/12/30/7505542/cas-dismisses-barcelona-transfer-ban-appeal|title=CAS dismisses Barcelona transfer ban appeal. |publisher=Goal.com |date=30 December 2014 |access-date=31 December 2014}}</ref>

===January===
Barcelona's new year started on 4 January with an away match against [[Real Sociedad]] at [[Anoeta Stadium]]. A poor start for Barcelona as they lost the match 1–0. An own goal from Jordi Alba decided the result.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/real-sociedad-v-fc-barcelona-barca-fall-at-anoeta-1-0|title=Barcelona fall at Anoeta. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=4 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015}}</ref> On 5 January, Barcelona announced that they had terminated the contract of director of football [[Andoni Zubizarreta]]. He had been sacked after serving for more than four years starting from July 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-terminate-the-contract-of-andoni-zubizarreta-as-director-of-football|title=Barcelona terminated the contract of Andoni Zubizarreta. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=5 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2015/01/05/7684932/barcelona-terminate-zubizarreta-contract?ICID=HP_HN_HP_RI_1_3 |title=Zubizarreta's contract terminated by Barcelona. |publisher=Goal.com |date=5 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015}}</ref> On the same day, [[Carles Puyol]], the assistant director of football, quit his position.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2015/01/05/7687382/puyol-leaves-barcelona?ICID=HP_HN_HP_RI_0_3 |title=Puyol quits Barcelona. |publisher=Goal.com |date=5 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015}}</ref> On 7 January, club president [[Josep Maria Bartomeu]] called for early presidential election at the end of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/detail/article/bartomeu-calls-presidential-election|title=Bartomeu called for early presidential election. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=7 January 2015 |access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref>

On 8 January, Barcelona played the first leg of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Round of 16|Round of 16 of Copa del Rey]] against [[Elche CF|Elche]] at Camp Nou. Barça won the match 5–0 from a brace by Neymar and goals from Suárez, Alba and a penalty from Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-elche-cf-five-star-performance-5-0|title=Win at first leg of round of 16. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 January 2015 |access-date=8 January 2015}}</ref> On 11 January, Barcelona played against [[Atlético Madrid]] at Camp Nou, winning 3–1. Neymar, Suárez and Messi scored for Barça, and [[Mario Mandžukić]] reduced the gap from a penalty for Atlético.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-atletico-madrid-3-1-three-headed-monster-strikes-again|title=Three headed monster strikes again. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 January 2015 |access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> On 15 January, Barcelona played against Elche in the second leg of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Round of 16|Round of 16 of Copa del Rey]] at [[Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero]]. Despite resting many first team players, Barca won 4–0 as Jérémy Mathieu, Sergi Roberto, Pedro and Adriano scored.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/copa-del-rey/1-8-2nd-leg/elx-cf_fc-barcelona|title=Barca through to quarter final. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=15 January 2015 |access-date=16 January 2015}}</ref> With the win, Barça were through to the [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Quarter-finals|Quarter-finals of Copa del Rey]] with an aggregate 9–0 victory.

On 18 January, Barça took on Deportivo at [[Estadio Riazor]], the last match of the first half of La Liga. Barca won the match 0–4 from Messi's hat-trick and an own goal by [[Sidnei (footballer, born 1989)|Sidnei]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-19/deportivo-de-la-coruna_fc-barcelona|title=Win at A Coruña. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 January 2015 |access-date=18 January 2015}}</ref> It was Messi's 22nd career hat-trick in La Liga. On 21 January, the first leg of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals of Copa del Rey]] took place between Barcelona and Atlético Madrid at Camp Nou, where Barça won 1–0 thanks to a late goal from Messi.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-v-atletico-madrid-messi-breaks-the-deadlock-1-0|title=Messi breaks the deadlock. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 January 2015 |access-date=21 January 2015}}</ref> On 24 January, Barca played against Elche at [[Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero]]. Barça won the match 0–6 as Messi and Neymar scored braces and Pedro and Piqué each scored once.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-20/elche_fc-barcelona|title=Convincing win by six goals. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 January 2015 |access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> Barça defeated Atlético Madrid in the second leg of the [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals of Copa del Rey]] 2–3 goals on 28 January at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]], completing a 4–2 aggregate win. Neymar scored a brace and [[Miranda (footballer, born 1984)|Miranda]] scored an own goal for Barcelona, while [[Fernando Torres]] and [[Raúl García (footballer, born 1986)|Raúl García]] scored for Atlético.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/atletico-de-madrid-v-fc-barcelona-2-3-triumphant-march-into-semis|title=Into the semis of Copa. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 January 2015 |access-date=29 January 2015}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Barcelona played the 21st match of La Liga against Villarreal at Camp Nou. Barça won the thrilling encounter 3-2 thanks to goals from Neymar, Rafinha and Messi; [[Denis Cheryshev]] and [[Luciano Vietto]] scored for Villarreal.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-21/fc-barcelona_villarreal|title=A thrilling encounter against Villarreal |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=1 February 2015 |access-date=2 February 2015}}</ref> On 8 February, Barcelona played Athletic Bilbao at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]] in [[Bilbao]]. Barcelona won the match 5–2 as Messi, Luis Suárez, Neymar and Pedro scored. The other Barcelona goal was an own goal by [[Óscar de Marcos]], while [[Mikel Rico]] and [[Aritz Aduriz]] reduced the gap for Athletic.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-22/athletic-club_fc-barcelona|title=Wild win in Bilbao. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 February 2015 |access-date=8 February 2015}}</ref> On 11 February, Barcelona played Villarreal in the first leg of [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Semi-finals|semi-finals of Copa del Rey]] at Camp Nou. Barça won the match 3–1 as Messi, Iniesta and Piqué scored for Barcelona, while Manu Trigueros scored for Villarreal. Neymar, meanwhile, missed a penalty.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/copa-del-rey/1-2-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_vila-real-c-f|title=Final in reach. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 February 2015 |access-date=11 February 2015}}</ref>

On 15 February, Barcelona played the 23rd match of La Liga against Levante at the Camp Nou. It was Messi's 300th La Liga appearance. Barcelona won the match 5–0 as Messi scored his 23rd La Liga hat-trick, while Neymar and Suárez scored one each.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-23/fc-barcelona_llevant-u-d|title=Winning streak continues against Levante.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=15 February 2015 |access-date=16 February 2015}}</ref> On 21 February, Barça's eleven-match winning streak came to an end as they lost to Málaga, 1–0. [[Juanmi (footballer, born 1993)|Juanmi]] scored the only goal at Camp Nou.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-24/fc-barcelona_malaga-cf|title=Eleven match winning streak ended against Malaga. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 February 2015 |access-date=21 February 2015}}</ref> On 25 February, FC Barcelona flew to the [[City of Manchester Stadium|Etihad Stadium]] in [[Manchester]] to play the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Manchester City v Barcelona|first leg of the Champions League Round of 16]] against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. Barça won the game 2–1 thanks to a brace from Suárez. [[Sergio Agüero]] reduced the gap for City in the second half of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d802dfe20c2-ecec11f0e813-1000--suarez-at-the-double-as-barcelona-win-at-city/|title=Suarez gives Barca victory at Etihad. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=25 February 2014 |access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref> On 28 February, Barcelona took on [[Granada CF|Granada]] at the [[Estadio Nuevo Los Cármenes]]. The ''Blaugranes'' won the match 3–1. The goals were scored by Rakitić and Suárez. [[Fran Rico]] scored for Granada, however Messi ensured Barça's victory by scoring his 27th league goal of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-25/granada-c-f_fc-barcelona|title=Win against Granada. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 February 2015 |access-date=28 February 2015}}</ref>

===March===
On 4 March, Barcelona played the [[2014–15 Copa del Rey#Semi-finals|second leg of semi-finals of Copa del Rey]] against Villarreal at El Madrigal. Barça won the match 1–3 and went through to the final by a 6–2 aggregate scoreline. Neymar scored a brace while Suárez added one; Jonathan dos Santos scored the only goal for Villarreal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/copa-del-rey/1-2-2nd-leg/vila-real-c-f_fc-barcelona|title=To the final of Copa del Rey.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=4 March 2015 |access-date=5 March 2015}}</ref> On 8 March, Barça played the 26th match of La Liga against Rayo Vallecano at Camp Nou, winning 6–1 as Messi scored his 24th La Liga hat-trick, Suárez scored a brace and Piqué scored the other. [[Alberto Bueno]] reduced the gap from a penalty while Dani Alves was sent off. With his hat-trick, Messi set the record for most hat-tricks in the history of La Liga. Additionally, Barcelona climbed to the top position of the league table with this win.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-26/fc-barcelona_rayo-vallecano|title=Barça at the top of the table. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 March 2015 |access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref>

On 14 March, Barça took on Eibar at the [[Ipurua Municipal Stadium]]. Messi scored both goals as Barça won 0–2.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-27/eibar_fc-barcelona|title=Win at Ipurua. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=14 March 2015 |access-date=15 March 2015}}</ref> On 18 March, Barça faced Manchester City at home for the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|second leg of Champions League round of 16]]. Barça won 1–0 on a goal by Rakitić, and as a result, Barcelona qualified for the quarter-final with a 3–1 aggregate score.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/021f-0e9afa44ad65-bff12e6d899f-1000--barcelona-get-past-city-despite-hart-heroics/|title=Barca at Champions League quarters. |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=18 March 2014 |access-date=19 March 2014}}</ref> Barcelona were drawn with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] draw. The second ''El Clásico'' of the Liga season was held on 22 March, during which Barcelona defeated their archrivals 2–1 at Camp Nou. The opener from Jérémy Mathieu was canceled out by Cristiano Ronaldo, but Suárez ensured a victory for Barcelona after scoring his team's second. Mathieu scored the first goal of his Barça career on the match. The win gave Barça a four-point lead over [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-28/fc-barcelona_reial-madrid-cf|title=Convincing win at El Clasico. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=22 March 2015 |access-date=23 March 2015}}</ref>

===April===
On 5 April, Barcelona played their 29th La Liga match at the [[Balaídos]] and won 0–1 against Celta Vigo, with the only goal scored by Mathieu.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-29/celta-de-vigo_fc-barcelona|title=Celta Vigo 0-1 Barca. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=5 April 2015 |access-date=6 April 2015}}</ref> On 8 April, Barça took on Almería at Camp Nou, defeating the visitors 4–0, as Suárez scored a brace and Messi and [[Marc Bartra]] scored one each.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-30/fc-barcelona_ud-almeria|title=Barca's comfy win at Camp Nou. |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=8 April 2015 |access-date=9 April 2015}}</ref> On 11 April, Barcelona played against Sevilla at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]]. The teams drew 2–2, which saw Barcelona's table lead fall to two points.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-31/sevilla_fc-barcelona|title=Barca wasted 2 crucial points. Score: 2-2|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=11 April 2015 |access-date=12 April 2015}}</ref>

On 15 April, Barcelona flew to the [[Parc des Princes]] in [[Paris]] to play the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals against Paris Saint-Germain. Barça won the game 1–3 via a brace from Suárez and a goal from Neymar. Mathieu reduced the gap for PSG by scoring an own goal in the second half of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2015/apr/15/psg-barcelona-champions-league-live|title=Barcelona clinched an important victory in 1st Leg.|publisher=Theguardian.com |date=15 April 2015 |access-date=15 April 2015}}</ref> On 18 April, Barcelona took on Valencia at home, winning 2–0 after an opening goal by Suárez and a late goal by Messi in the injury time, his 400th career goal for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-32/fc-barcelona_valencia|title=Barcelona beat Valencia by 2-0 |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=18 April 2015 |access-date=19 April 2015}}</ref> On 21 April, Barca took on PSG at the Camp Nou for the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|second leg of Champions League quarter-finals]]. Neymar scored both goals as Barça won 2–0, thus qualifying for the semi-finals with a 5–1 aggregate score. With victory, Barcelona reached the Champions League semi-finals for the seventh time in the last eight years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/champions-league/1-4-2nd-leg/fc-barcelona_psg|title=Barcelona in Champions League semifinals.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 April 2015 |access-date=21 April 2015}}</ref>

Barcelona were drawn with [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Semi-finals|semi-finals]] during the semi-final draw in [[Nyon]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0220-0e9066b57ea2-607cb7808487-1000--guardiola-takes-bayern-to-barca-madrid-get-juve/|title=Barcelona vs Bayern Munich.|publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=24 April 2015 |access-date=24 April 2015}}</ref> On 25 April, Barcelona defeated Espanyol 0–2 at the [[RCDE Stadium|Cornellà-El Prat]] and won the second [[Derbi barceloní|derby]] of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-33/espanyol_fc-barcelona|title=Comfy Derby win.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=25 April 2015 |access-date=25 April 2015}}</ref> On 28 April, Barça played its 34th match of the league season against Getafe at the Camp Nou, winning 6–0 as Messi and Suárez each scored a brace and Neymar and Xavi each got a goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-34/fc-barcelona_getafe|title=Barca smashed Getafe by 6-0.|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=28 April 2015 |access-date=28 April 2015}}</ref>

===May===
On 2 May, Barcelona took on Córdoba at [[Estadio Nuevo Arcángel]]. Barcelona won the match 0–8 as Suárez scored his first Barcelona hat-trick, Messi scored twice and Neymar, Rakitić and Piqué each scored one. Messi had a chance to score a hat-trick when Córdoba conceded a penalty but he gave the chance to Neymar, who duly obliged.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-35/cordoba_fc-barcelona|title=Barca punished Cordoba by 8-0 |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=2 May 2015 |access-date=2 May 2015}}</ref> On 6 May, Barcelona played the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Semi-finals|first leg of the semi-finals of the Champions League]] against Bayern Munich, winning 3–0 as Messi scored twice in three minutes and assisted for Neymar, who scored one in injury time.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/champions-league/1-2-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_bayern-munich|title=Messi's Magic gives Barca 3-0 lead over Bayern Munich |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=6 May 2015 |access-date=6 May 2015}}</ref> Messi's second goal in the match won the UEFA Goal of the Year award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/goal-of-the-season/result/ |title=Messi bamboozles Bayern - Goal of the Season – UEFA.com |website=[[UEFA]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150829233742/http://www.uefa.com/goal-of-the-season/result |archive-date=2015-08-29}}</ref>

On 9 May, Barcelona played the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15 La Liga 36th matchday]] at Camp Nou against [[Real Sociedad]], a game Barça won 2–0, with Neymar scoring the first with a header and Pedro scoring the second goal with a bicycle kick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-36/fc-barcelona_real-sociedad|title=Barcelona vs Real Sociedad : 2-0 |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=9 May 2015 |access-date=9 May 2015}}</ref> With the win, Barcelona were one win away from winning the 2014–15 La Liga title as they were four points above Real Madrid with only two games left.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-close-in-on-2014-15-la-liga-title|title=Barcelona close in on 2014-15 La Liga title |publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=9 May 2015 |access-date=9 May 2015}}</ref> On 12 May, Barcelona flew to the [[Allianz Arena]] in [[Munich]] to play the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Semi-finals|second leg of the semi-finals of the Champions League]] against Bayern Munich. Neymar scored both goals in a 2–3 Barça loss, though the team nonetheless won 5–3 on aggregate and booked their place in the final of Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/champions-league/1-2-2nd-leg/bayern-munich_fc-barcelona|title=Barcelona in the final of Champions League|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=12 May 2015 |access-date=12 May 2015}}</ref> On 17 May, Barcelona clinched their 23rd La Liga title after winning 0–1 against Atlético Madrid at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium|Vicente Calderón]]. The game's only goal, by Messi, was enough to win the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/title-league-champions-fcbarcelona-atletico-madrid-2014-15|title=Barcelona are La Liga Champions|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=17 May 2015|access-date=17 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519225125/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/title-league-champions-fcbarcelona-atletico-madrid-2014-15|archive-date=19 May 2015|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> This was Barcelona's seventh La Liga title in the last ten years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-s-seventh-league-title-in-ten-years|title=Seventh La Liga title in last ten years|publisher=FCBarcelona.com|date=17 May 2015|access-date=17 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519110212/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/fc-barcelona-s-seventh-league-title-in-ten-years|archive-date=19 May 2015|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> On 21 May, Xavi had announced that he will leave Barcelona at the end of the season for [[Al-Sadd]] in [[Qatar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/xavi-hernandez-it-s-time-to-go|title=Xavi Hernández: It's time to go|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=21 May 2015 |access-date=21 May 2015}}</ref>

On 23 May, Barcelona played the final match of La Liga against Deportivo at Camp Nou; Messi scored twice in the 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/league/round-38/fc-barcelona_deportivo-de-la-coruna|title=Barca vs Deportivo 2-2|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=23 May 2015 |access-date=23 May 2015}}</ref> This was Xavi's last La Liga match. On 30 May, Barca took on Athletic Bilbao to play the [[2015 Copa del Rey Final|final of the Copa del Rey]] at the Camp Nou. Barcelona won the match 3–1, clinching their 27th title. Messi scored twice, with the other scored by Neymar.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2014-2015/copa-del-rey/final/athletic-club_fc-barcelona|title=Barca won 27th title of Copa Del Rey|publisher=FCBarcelona.com |date=30 May 2015 |access-date=30 May 2015}}</ref> Messi's first goal was scored through an impressive dribble on the right flank. The move started with Messi close to the half-way line. Cornered by four Bilbao players, Messi burst on and managed to beat them all with abnormal ease before running towards the goal and calmly slotting the ball past the goalkeeper. Messi's goal was subsequently nominated for the [[FIFA Puskás Award]], an award given to the best goal of the year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/puskas-award-2015-lionel-messi-alessandro|title=florenzi-and-wendell-lira-nominated-for-goal-of-the-year-a67|website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |accessdate=3 December 2022}}</ref>

===June===
[[File:Moment of the Champions League final FC Barcelona - Juventus 2015.jpg|thumb|right|Messi challenging [[Patrice Evra]] in the [[2015 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League Final]]]]
On 6 June, Barcelona played the [[2015 UEFA Champions League Final]] against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] with the opportunity for both teams to complete the [[Treble (association football)|continental treble]], after having already won their domestic league and cup competitions, respectively. Barcelona clinched their fifth Champions League trophy, and fourth in the last ten seasons, with a 3–1 victory over ''I bianconeri'' at the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]] in [[Berlin]]. Barcelona completed the historic treble with goals from Rakitić, Suárez and Neymar. By accomplishing this feat, Barcelona became the only [[UEFA|European]] club to have won the treble twice.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ie/match/juventus-vs-barcelona/1700349/report|title=Juventus 1 Barcelona 3 |date=6 June 2015|work=Goal.com|access-date=10 November 2015}}</ref> With the win, Barcelona qualified for the [[2015 UEFA Super Cup]] against the [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League]] winners Sevilla, to be played in August 2015.
